title: UNHCR announces that one million people have fled Ukraine in one week
body:
On 3 March 2022, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Filippo Grandi, announced that about one million people had fled Ukraine in the seven days since Russia's full-scale invasion began on 24 February 2022. In a statement reported by UN News, Grandi called the conflict a "senseless war" and said that in nearly 40 years of work in refugee emergencies he had rarely seen an exodus that fast.

Most of the people leaving Ukraine crossed into Poland. Others entered Hungary, Moldova, Romania and Slovakia, the other countries bordering Ukraine to the west and south. According to the same report, many more people had also been displaced inside Ukraine.

Grandi warned that millions more could flee unless the fighting ended immediately. He argued that "Peace is the only way to halt this tragedy." UNHCR, the UN refugee agency, subsequently began publishing running counts of refugees from Ukraine recorded in European host countries, drawing on figures supplied by national authorities. The one-million milestone, reached within a single week, became an early reference point for the scale of the displacement caused by the invasion, and the agency's later statements on the war continued to be framed around the number of people who had left the country and the number displaced within it.
